title: finding(forms): the CRM example and the submit route's docstring say the `guest_portal` profile authorizes an anonymous form submit; measured on 17.7.0, it does not
body:
Found by the `repo:www.objectos.ai` seat (objectstack-ai/objectstack#12224) while staging www.objectos.ai#272, a post on public form intake, on 2026-10-17. Measured on the published `@objectstack/cli` **17.7.0** against `examples/app-crm` taken from tag `@objectstack/cli@17.7.0`. **Class b:** the comments an AI author reads contradict both the docs and the runtime.

## What disagrees

| Source | What it says |
| :--- | :--- |
| `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx:13` | "Declare a public form view; the submit route derives a narrow authorization from that declaration. No `guest` profile, no broad grant." |
| `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:11102-11107` and `packages/plugin-security` `security-plugin.ts:2334-2336` (at the tag) | Both agree with the docs: the `publicFormGrant` works **without** `guest_portal`. |
| `examples/app-crm/src/views/lead.view.ts:96-104` (tag; `:95-106` on `origin/main` 570c7a2d95) | "the `guest_portal` profile (INSERT-only on crm_lead) authorizes the write". |
| `examples/app-crm/src/security/sales-positions.ts:59-66` (tag; `:63-73` on main) | "Applied to anonymous … visitors who POST the public form". |
| `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:10702-10706` (tag; `:9066-9071` on main), the route docstring | "Security is delegated to the `guest_portal` permission set … If the deployment hasn't registered a `guest_portal` profile, the security middleware falls open". |

## Measured

The seat removed `GuestPortalProfile` from the CRM's `permissions`. The build refused with an access-matrix drift, which was accepted with `--update-access-matrix`, leaving one permission set in the artifact. It then re-ran the same probes. Every answer was identical to the run with the profile in place:

| Probe | Answer |
| :--- | :--- |
| Clean POST | `201` |
| POST smuggling `status`, `owner_id` and `organization_id` | `201`, with the same stripping |
| Anonymous list | `401` |
| Anonymous read of the created row | `401` |

## Why it matters

An agent that copies the CRM example adds a `guest_portal` profile it does not need. An agent that reads the docstring can conclude that a deployment without the profile "falls open", which is the opposite of what the runtime does.

A stale pointer sits next to it. `rest-server.ts:11028-11029` (at the tag) names `lead.hook.ts` / `case.hook.ts` in app-crm as the canonical defaults-stamping pattern. Neither file exists at the tag: `src/hooks/` holds only `opportunity.hook.ts`.

## Done looks like

- The example's comments and the route docstring state the mechanism the docs and the runtime implement. The example either drops `GuestPortalProfile` or says why it keeps it.
- The stale hook-file pointer is corrected.
- If `guest_portal` still has a real role on this path, for example the `permissions: ['guest_portal']` the submit context carries, the docs say what that role is.

Related, not duplicated: #22437 (the 201 read-back, closed) and #6920 (section-less forms, closed).
